title: Speed exact Eisenstein floor replay with integer-pair rank
head: 3bab32433b1a78a0b692619eb0ac8a5ab2ec6b2b
body:
The complete Eisenstein floor verifier spends much of its runtime in exact Fraction rank arithmetic. This adds an **optional source-authenticated integer-pair K-rank adapter** for all 359 calls over `K=Q(omega)`, preserving the unchanged verifier's entire output and seven original negative controls. Its 311 F4 and 209 Q calls retain their original implementations. No frozen source, existing verifier, selected record or mathematical claim is changed.

Six alternating fresh-process timing pairs on CPython 3.12.7/Windows, after warmup, gave these medians:

| Identical fixture | Original | Integer K-rank | Ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complete replay, including imports/authentication | 1.43271 s | 1.20969 s | 1.184x |
| All 359 actual K-rank calls | 0.485263 s | 0.057389 s | 8.456x |

Every complete stdout byte stream matched. Timed matrices are frozen copies whose ordered digest must equal the verified actual-call census; the receipt also records adapter hashes and all timing observations. Concurrent machine load was uncontrolled, and no universal speed or CI improvement is claimed. The full observed ranges were 1.14770–2.24239 s and 0.85541–1.56985 s. Timing is evidence, not a passing threshold.

The proof uses standard exact row operations: clear each row's rational denominators, eliminate with nonzero pivot multiplication and subtraction over integer pairs, then divide out common integer content. All operations preserve K-rank. No numerical tolerance, modular rank inference or mathematical-result cache is used. A separate restriction-of-scalars checker expands each K entry to a two-by-two rational block and passes 9,009 matrices, checking `rank_Q=2*rank_K` without importing the retained rank function.

Use the adapter:

```sh
python3.12 -I -O -B research/eisenstein-integer-rank/replay.py
```

Validate its complete evidence:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/eisenstein-integer-rank
```

The registered CPython 3.12.7 suite passed: every actual K-call comparison, complete-output equality, eight new controls, independent rational rank checks, Git-free full replay, both source corruptions rejected before import, and a bool/int receipt mutation. A separate AI reviewer read the proof, algorithm and adapter, then independently passed optimized CPython 3.12.14 primary and 9,009-matrix checks with no blocker. No human review, hosted CI, selected full replay or proof-assistant result is claimed.

Base and refreshed main are `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. The sole draw `f8bcc67b513a3d69bbc4e37e0216af2b` selected verifier engineering; TASK records the refined `replay-runtime` scope and required baseline pass. Final overlap includes the complete cached 798 open PRs and 1,252 Discussion records at 15:55/15:59 UTC, plus 50 current updated open PRs and exact PR2017/2537/2552/2506 bodies at 16:10 UTC. PR2537 accelerates rational nullspace output in a different initializer; this is quadratic-field rank with no returned basis. PR2607's adaptive affine floor is a separate mathematical result.

Credit Jose Manuel (@jmbarrancoml) for PR2017's full verifier and proof, and Jonathan Lam, Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled for the retained geometry. Their source notices remain untouched. Primitive integer elimination and restriction of scalars are standard methods. New profiling, adapter and verification work is by **ywz65**, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, testing, writing and review. Apache-2.0. No new supplier, pairing bound or kappa.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
